definitions.explanation: The same size as the real object, with no enlargement or reduction. Used for reproductions, models, and prints.

examples.japanese: {原寸大|げんすんだい}の{模型|もけい}を{作|つく}る。
この{写真|しゃしん}は{原寸大|げんすんだい}で{印刷|いんさつ}されている。
examples.english: This photo is printed at actual size.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}に{恐竜|きょうりゅう}の{原寸大|げんすんだい}レプリカが{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: A life-size dinosaur replica is on display at the museum.

notes:
Composed of {原寸|げんすん} (original dimensions) + {大|だい} (size), where {原|げん} means 'original' and {寸|すん} is a traditional unit of measurement. Often used as a modifier: {原寸大|げんすんだい}の.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {原寸大|げんすんだい}の{模型|もけい}: a full-size model
- {原寸大|げんすんだい}で{再現|さいげん}する: to reproduce at actual size
- {原寸大|げんすんだい}レプリカ: a life-size replica
- {原寸大|げんすんだい}で{印刷|いんさつ}する: to print at actual size

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {等身大|とうしんだい}: life-size (of a person) — specifically refers to human-sized figures or statues; also used figuratively to mean 'true to life' or 'unembellished'
- {実物大|じつぶつだい}: actual size, real-size — very similar to {原寸大|げんすんだい}; can be used interchangeably in most contexts
- {縮小|しゅくしょう}: reduction, scaled down — the opposite concept
